results.title: Poisson ideal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket $\lbrace \cdot, \cdot \rbrace$. An ideal $P$ of $A$ is a Poisson ideal when $\lbrace a, p \rbrace \in P$ for all $a \in A$ and all $p \in P$.

results.title: Poisson prime ideal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. An ideal $P$ of $A$ is a Poisson prime when it is both a prime ideal and a Poisson ideal.

results.title: Poisson core
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. For an ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is the supremum, in the lattice of ideals of $A$, of the set of all Poisson ideals of $A$ contained in $J$.

results.title: Bracket with zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket $\lbrace \cdot, \cdot \rbrace$. For every $a \in A$, $\lbrace a, 0 \rbrace = 0$.

results.title: The zero ideal is a Poisson ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. The zero ideal of $A$ is a Poisson ideal.

results.title: The sum of two Poisson ideals inside an ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket, and let $I$, $K$ and $J$ be ideals of $A$. If $I$ and $K$ are Poisson ideals contained in $J$, then their sum $I + K$ is a Poisson ideal contained in $J$.

results.title: The Poisson core is a Poisson ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is a Poisson ideal.

results.title: The Poisson core is contained in the ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is contained in $J$.

results.title: Poisson ideals inside an ideal lie in its Poisson core
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket, and let $J$ and $P$ be ideals of $A$. If $P \subseteq J$ and $P$ is a Poisson ideal, then $P$ is contained in the Poisson core of $J$.

results.title: Universal property of the Poisson core
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is the greatest element of the set of Poisson ideals of $A$ contained in $J$: it is a Poisson ideal contained in $J$, and it contains every Poisson ideal of $A$ contained in $J$.

results.title: Spoof factorizations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite multiset $F = \{(x_1, a_1), \dots, (x_r, a_r)\}$ of pairs of natural numbers, read as the formal product $x_1^{a_1} \cdots x_r^{a_r}$, is a spoof factorization if every base $x_i$ and every exponent $a_i$ is positive.

results.title: Spoof evaluation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F = x_1^{a_1} \cdots x_r^{a_r}$ be a finite multiset of pairs $(x_i, a_i)$ of natural numbers, each a base $x_i$ with an exponent $a_i$. The spoof evaluation of $F$ is the integer $\tilde e(F) = x_1^{a_1} \cdots x_r^{a_r} = \prod_{i=1}^{r} x_i^{a_i}$.

results.title: Spoof totient
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite multiset of pairs $(x_i, a_i)$ of natural numbers, $i = 1, \dots, r$, viewed as the formal product $x_1^{a_1} \cdots x_r^{a_r}$. The spoof totient of $F$ is the integer $\tilde\varphi(F) = \prod_{i=1}^{r} (x_i^{a_i} - x_i^{a_i - 1})$, where the exponent $a_i - 1$ is truncated at $0$, so a pair with $a_i = 0$ contributes the factor $0$.

results.title: Spoof evaluation and spoof totient of $3 \cdot 3$

results.title: Solutions of the Lehmer equation

results.title: The multiset $\{3, 3\}$ solves the Lehmer equation

So $\{3, 3\}$ solves Equation (1), the equation $k \prod_j (x_j - 1) = \prod_j x_j - 1$ in the elements $x_j$ of a multiset, counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Bound on unitary Lehmer factorizations
results.caption: Theorem
